These form a triadic constraint system where D ≥ 1, A = 1, and C ≥ 0.95 define valid operational states. Failure occurs when any component violates its regime. For instance, if D < 1, definitions are unstable and risk model drift. If A = 0, no infrastructure supports managed storage, necessitating rollback. If C < 0.95, inconsistency undermines trust in predictions. The system operates under a dual logic: use when all gates open, reject otherwise. Each primitive maps to a distinct layer—mathematical structure in GSI, operational state in GSE—ensuring coherence across abstraction levels.
